Since 2017, there has been a revival program underway to bring the language back. == Classification == Once included in the [[Kuric languages]], Bowern (2011) classifies Nganyaywana as a separate '''[[Anēwan]]''' (Anaiwan) branch of the Pama–Nyungan languages.Bowern, Claire. 2011. "[http://anggarrgoon.wordpress.com/2011/12/23/how-many-languages-were-spoken-in-australia/ How Many Languages Were Spoken in Australia?]", ''Anggarrgoon: Australian languages on the web'', 23 December 2011 ([http://pamanyungan.sites.yale.edu/master-list-australian-languages-v12 corrected] 6 February 2012) ==Dialects== Besides Nganyaywana, Anewan may include '''Enneewin''', with which shares about 65% of its vocabulary.
